Public admission calls share the single admissionCycle until that cycle settles. No later cycle can replace it before its own finally runs, so admissionCycle === cycle is true at this cleanup site under the implemented serialization.

No private-map assertion was added solely to kill these variants. This is a scoped policy observation, not unconditional internal-state/work equivalence.

Removing activeExtension reset can make the first successful renewal block all later renewals. Current gated tests hold that first extension until stop and therefore do not require a second successful heartbeat during a continuing invocation.

Replacing the half-lease interval with its minimum can schedule renewal every millisecond instead of half the lease. Existing pending-renewal tests prevent overlap, which can hide this extra pacing/load. Assert no renewal before the intended boundary and repeated healthy pacing in a follow-up.

Removing unref can keep an otherwise idle process alive while an owner abandons a live invocation. Tests dispose their owned resources and do not use a subprocess liveness harness. This process-lifetime behavior is not equivalent merely because unit tests exit normally.
